decisions.reason: The DCDC1 3.4V compensation and Schottky OR-ing semantics are already fully recorded by the candidate's existing message-434 MODIFY.
The candidate already has a complete message-434 MODIFY recording the 3.4V programmed output and its diode-drop compensation purpose.
Programming DCDC1 to 3.4V before the Schottky drop does not change the monitoring device, monitored rails, monitor position, or downstream measurement coverage.
The voltage-compensation decision does not change the number, identity, or separation of project boards.
The source introduces a power-button connector but establishes no placement, orientation, clearance, or accessibility change for the existing battery and interboard connectors.
Neither the DCDC1 setting nor the new button connector clause changes the established board dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, or enclosure-fit constraints.
The source decision does not alter the power board's four-layer stack.
The DCDC1 voltage compensation and panel power-button connector do not change the charge-status LED interface or its electrical parameters.

The panel-mounted power-control behavior is already independently and completely introduced from message 434; the source Requirement's DCDC1-related modification requires no additional candidate MODIFY.
The source decision changes normal-operation power conditioning but does not alter USB data routing, enumeration, flashing, or standalone-programming behavior.
The LEDs remain powered from the separate 5V rail, so the DCDC1 3.4V compensation does not change their supply, level shifting, part selection, or control.
The source changes the AXP2101 DCDC1 path for the 3.3V system rail, not the separate MT3608 5V boost rail or its enable behavior.
